title.narrative: EU Green Agenda in Serbia: biodiversity and water for climate resilience
EU:s Gröna Agenda i Serbien: biodiversitet, vatten och klimatresiliens

description.narrative:
Huvudsyftet med projektet är att förbättra styrning och förvaltning av ekosystem genom ökad kapacitet för planering, genomförande och upprätthållande av natur-, vatten- och klimatpolitik i Serbien senast 2026.
Projektet kommer att stödja EU:s miljöreform och ett effektivt, inkluderande och hållbart genomförande av EU:s gröna agenda i Serbien. Projektet kommer att ge fokus till biologisk mångfald, vatten och våtmarker och klimatmotståndskraft, genom att stärka policy och basvillkor, stödja fortsatt arbete med Nature Based Solutions (NbS) genom pilotprojekt och främja möjligheter för mobilisering och uppskalning av klimat- och biologisk mångfaldsfinansiering. Projektet syftar till att bygga kapacitet, tvärsektoriellt samarbete och en samhällelig dialog samt bygga starka partnerskap mellan offentlig sektor, privata företag och civilsamhället, för att påskynda en grön omställning.

The main objective of the project is to improve governance and management of ecosystems through increased capacities for planning, implementation and enforcement of nature, water and climate policies in Serbia by 2026.
The Project will support the EU environmental reform and efficient, inclusive and sustainable implementation the EU Green Agenda in Serbia. The Project will give focus to biodiversity, water and wetlands and climate resilience, by strengthening policy and base-conditions, supporting further work on Nature Based Solutions (NbS) through pilot projects and promote opportunities for mobilization and scale-up of climate and biodiversity financing. The Project aims at building capacity, cross-sectorial cooperation a societal dialogue as well as building strong partnerships between the public sector, private companies and civil society, to accelerate green transformation.

At the Board meeting in May 2024 the achievements under the first full year spanning December 2022 to December 2023 of project implementation, and progress made in form of results towards the project goals, were presented and discussed.
Some noteworthy results are presented below:
- New Decree on Ecological Network (drafted under this project) received the green light from the Ministry of Environmental Protection (MEP), marking a crucial step forward in the commitment to strengthening the governance relevant for wetlands, and more importantly protected areas and ecological corridors.
- Further legislative improvement in the realm of nature protection in the development of an ex-post analysis for the Law on Nature Protection.
- Recognizing the importance of robust data infrastructure, an Assessment Report on the needs for upgrading the field research application (TERENSKA), with elements relevant for wetland conservation was completed.
- Enhanced the technical capacities for biodiversity data storage and exchange at both the Institute for Nature Conservation of Serbia (INCS) and the Provincial Institute for Nature Conservation (PINC) through acquisition and transfer of the first batch of IT equipment to these institutions, in line with identified priority needs.
- 3 comprehensive training sessions were organized: the training on Copernicus Services and Sectoral Information System (SIS) with 122 participants, the training on the use of the Climate Atlas of Serbia and the Disaster Risk Registry with 49 participants, as well as the online training session on Nature-based Solutions conducted in collaboration with Naturvårdsverket with 124 participants.
- As the focus of the project is on the implementation of NbS in protected wetlands, the draft of the upcoming Challenge Call for innovative project proposals was prepared. With the future project proposals in mind and the potential sites for their implementation, a field visit to the RAMSAR site, the Special Nature Reserve "Pestersko polje," with representatives of MEP, INCS and the protected area management was carried out. In addition a formal assessment of potential sites through the engagement of a national consultant who is evaluating at least 10 protected areas with wetlands for the implementation of Nature based Solutions.
- Regarding communications and in order to reach out to the wider audience, the project communicated the strategic vision of the project during the Project Kick-Off event, and developed a comprehensive communications plan to guide future outreach activities. UNDP project team also joined two seminars organized by MEP for protected area managers in order to engage with stakeholders, foster a dialogue and announce opportunities that will be available through this project.
